Hi Alex, Lauren —

Appreciate the call today — looping in some details so you have a head start before Thu: 

High-level network options we support (summary):
- Option A: Customer-managed VPC endpoints (recommended for highest isolation). We provide a private IP-range and route tables instructions; egress is through your VPC.
- Option B: IP allowlist to Redwood-managed VPC endpoints (simpler, less infra work). Good for POC or teams that cannot set up endpoints immediately.
- Option C: Hybrid — staging via allowlist, production via customer VPC endpoints + mTLS.

Auth & tooling: 
- Staging: API keys + IP allowlist (short lived API keys available).
- Production: we support mTLS for the control plane and TLS client auth for data-plane; we also offer a token-exchange flow with short-lived bearer tokens backed by your IdP (OIDC).
- Key management: Redwood integrates with customer KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) for model keying and can provide HSM-backed options.

Embedding & storage: 
- By default embeddings are stored in Redwood-managed vector stores to enable efficient reranking. Export: customers can request a full export; we also support connector-based sync to your managed DB (S3/GCS/BigQuery) for compliance. Retention is configurable by policy.

Network specifics to prepare for Thu call: 
- Do you have an IP allowlist range for staging?
- Will FinPay use DNS egress restrictions (e.g., only allow calls to specific hostnames)?
- Any existing mTLS cert provisioning system or preferred IdP for OIDC?

I'll attach the VPC checklist (see attachments) and a short architecture diagram (in the Drive link Lauren shared).

Cheers,

Hi Alex — quick technical notes ahead of Thu: 

IP allowlist vs VPC endpoints:
- Shared Redwood endpoints + IP allowlist: we allocate static egress IPs per region. Works well for staging but is less ideal for stricter compliance (auditability, network flow logs).
- Customer VPC endpoints: we support AWS PrivateLink and GCP Private Service Connect. For AWS PrivateLink we ask for the VPC CIDR and subnets where the endpoint will be created and we provide a service name to connect to.

Egress/DNS behavior:
- If your egress policy blocks non-approved FQDNs, you can allow: api.redwood.ai and s3.redwood.ai (for optional artifact upload). We also support custom hostname mappings for private deployments.

mTLS & cert rotation:
- We support mTLS for both control and data plane. Cert rotation can be automated via a small agent (if you want us to run a managed cert rotation) or via your PKI — we provide a rotation API and sample scripts.

Performance/routing notes for embeddings and rerankers:
- For reranking workflows, we recommend colocating your embedding store in the same region and enabling caching in the SDK. This reduces cross-region latency.
- SDK notes: our client SDK supports structured tool-calling and streaming; auth can be switched from API key to mTLS with minimal changes to the config object (examples available in the repo).

I'll bring config snippets and our PrivateLink service name on the call.

-Jonas
